references.text: Hosea refers directly to Jacob's struggle with the angel: he wrestled and wept and pleaded for mercy, a prophetic allusion to the event in Gen 32:26.
Explains the lasting consequence of Jacob's hip being dislocated during the struggle (v. 26): Israelites do not eat the thigh muscle.
Jacob refuses to let go until he is blessed and receives the name Israel because he has struggled with God and humans and prevailed.
Jesus' parable of the persistent widow illustrates the same principle as Jacob's struggle: holding on and not giving up until the blessing comes.
No one grabs hold of God and holds fast—a contrast to Jacob, who just grabbed hold of God and refused to let go.
This is the direct continuation of the same event that explains the origin of a ritual practice.
